structure: channels-outer (affine_range(2)) / state-inner (affine_range(16)); delta/u loaded once per channel tile; per-state: activation(exp,scale=A_i) on Scalar, tensor_tensor(delta,u,multiply), broadcast B_i, tensor_tensor_scan(deltaA,deltaBu,initial=0,mul,add), broadcast C_i, multiply, accumulate; store output per channel tile
notes: Phase 1: first correct kernel. Full 5-seed PASS with 0.832x baseline speedup (1.5116ms vs 1.258ms baseline). Surprise: HBMrd 72MB (expected 16MB floor; 4.5x above -> compiler spilling SBUF to HBM). PE=52%/Vec=51% co-limit, not purely Vector-bound as hypothesized. DMA=11% confirms NOT DMA-bound. Hypothesis for the regression vs baseline: the baseline's state-outer/channel-inner structure allocates scanC_accum as [n_channel_tile,128,seq_len] in one 3D array outside both loops, which may give the compiler better scheduling; our per-channel-tile local accum + whole-M tiles may trigger spilling. Phase 2 levers: (1) hoist deltaU out of state loop, (2) investigate spill (sequence tiling or structure matching baseline's allocation pattern).

structure: sequence-tiled seq-tile-INNER fallback: channels-outer (affine_range(2)) / state-mid (affine_range(16)) / seq-tile-inner (static_range(14) over tiles of 512); delta/u loaded whole-M once per channel tile; per-state scan_init=zeros([128,1]) carried via scan_init[...] = scan_res[0:128, seq_tile-1]; per-state: activation(exp,scale=A_i), tensor_tensor(delta,u), broadcast b, tensor_tensor_scan(deltaA,deltaBu,initial=scan_init), broadcast c, multiply, accumulate; store per channel tile. Mirrors profile/refs/ref_v3.py
notes: Phase 3 D1a S0-fallback screen (--fast seed 42). Spill eliminated (72MB->16MB). Correct 1/1. 0.8362ms/1.505x is SLOWER than the D1b seq-tile-outer lead (0.7828ms/1.607x) beyond noise, so D1b is promoted as mamba_v2 and this variant is recorded as a screen only (NOT promoted).

structure: sequence-tiled seq-tile-OUTER: sequential_range(14) over tiles of 512 (loop-carried); [n_channel_tile,128,S] scan_state carried across tiles; channels (affine_range(2)) then states (affine_range(16)) inside; initial = scan_state[i_ct,:,i_state] for tiles>0 else scalar 0; after scan write scan_res[:,seq_tile-1:seq_tile] into scan_state[i_ct,:,i_state:i_state+1]; per-seq-tile store (no whole-M accumulator). Mirrors profile/refs/ref_optimized.py
notes: Phase 3 PROMOTED. Full 5-seed PASS (correct 1/1). Sequence tiling kills the whole-M SBUF spill (HBMrd 72MB->16MB read-once floor) and lets the compiler pipeline PE against Vec (52/51%->99/89%): 1.5116ms->0.7822ms, 0.832x->1.609x. Faster than the D1a fallback (0.8362ms) beyond noise; seed-42 --fast screen 0.7828/1.607x consistent with the 5-seed 0.7822/1.609x. Math/fp32 semantics unchanged from mamba_v1 (only loop/tile structure). New bottleneck: PE=99% from the b/c partition-dim broadcast_to lowered to nc_matmul(ones,row); DMA idle at 12% -> the S1 off-PE-broadcast lever targets this.

structure: S1a: seq-tile-outer (sequential_range) + state-outer/channel-inner reorder; b[s,:]/c[s,:] materialized once per state into shared [128,seq_tile] B_bcast/C_bcast tiles reused across both channel tiles; delta/u preloaded into [n_ct,128,seq_tile] shared buffers; rest identical to mamba_v2
notes: S1a off-PE broadcast via channel-loop hoist. PE-active-time dropped 0.774ms->0.428ms (~halved, confirms sharing the broadcast across the 2 channel tiles removes ~half the nc_matmul broadcast work). BUT the state-outer reorder needed to share the broadcast exposes Vec as the new bottleneck (89%->97%, Vec-active 0.696->0.814ms) and latency REGRESSED 0.7822->0.8397ms (+7.3%). Per AC-5.1 keep/drop is latency-primary -> DROPPED. Correct 1/1 (rel-L2 fine, values identical). Lesson: in the channels-outer/seq-tile-outer structure the b/c broadcast is effectively hidden under the PE pipeline; reordering to share it costs more Vec than the PE it saves. Motivates S1b (DMA broadcast keeps the winning structure, moves broadcast to idle DMA).

structure: S1b: mamba_v2 structure with b/c partition broadcast replaced by a stride-0 partition-broadcast DMA from HBM: nisa.dma_copy(dst=B_bcast[p_idx,f_idx], src=b[i_state+p_idx*0, seq_start+f_idx]) with p_idx=arange(128)[:,None], f_idx=arange(512)[None,:]

notes: S1b HBM-source probe. Also rejected earlier spellings: broadcast_to on an HBM tile (needs SBUF/PSUM); .ap() on TensorView (sliced HBM view) and on TensorRef (kernel input) -- neither exposes .ap in neuronx-cc 2.0.260476. The Codex arange-index stride-0 idiom compiles the AP but the BIR code generator cannot lower the {0,+,0}[128] partition-broadcast DMA. Infeasible under the harness build; DROPPED per AC-5.2.

structure: S1b SBUF->SBUF fallback: nl.load b/c row into [1,W] SBUF (B_row/C_row), then nisa.dma_copy(dst=B_bcast[p_idx,f_idx], src=B_row[p_idx*0, f_idx]) stride-0 partition broadcast SBUF->SBUF

notes: S1b SBUF-source fallback probe. IDENTICAL compiler rejection as the HBM-source probe -> proves the {0,+,0}[128] stride-0 partition-broadcast DMA PATTERN itself is unsupported by BIR codegen in this build, independent of source memory space and independent of --disable-dge. Confirms S1b is conclusively infeasible; the S1 off-PE-broadcast lever fails entirely (S1a=latency regression, S1b=codegen-infeasible). mamba_v2 remains the winner.
S2 width sweep. Tied with 512 within noise (~0.1%). Scl climbs (23->35%) as tiles shrink (more, shorter exp calls) but stays hidden.
S2 width sweep. Nominally fastest (0.7814 vs 512's 0.7822) but the 0.1% delta is sub-noise (<< 3% promotion threshold; v2 same-session control band is ~0.1%). NOT promoted; 512 kept for stability.

S2 width sweep. REGRESSES vs 512 (0.7961 vs 0.7822). Wider tile lowers PE% (fewer b/c broadcast matmuls, as hypothesized) BUT latency rises: the longer per-tile scan dependency + rising Scl (exp over wider tiles) outweigh the PE saving.

S2 width sweep. REGRESSES most (0.8495/1.481x). Confirms MONOTONE widen-regression 512->896->1024; the 'wider wins' hypothesis (from PE-broadcast-count) is DISPROVEN. Sweep minimum is the flat 256/448/512 band; wider and finer both no better -> 512 hard-kept as optimal for M=7168. No edge-extend to 1792 (wider clearly worse) or 128 (256 already shows no gain) warranted.

structure: seq-tile-outer (sequential_range(14), tiles of 512) + state-outer/channel-inner reorder: b[s,:]/c[s,:] materialized once per state into shared [128,512] B_bcast/C_bcast reused across both channel tiles (S1a, halves partition-broadcast matmuls); deltaU=delta*u precomputed once per (seq-tile,channel-tile) into deltaU_ct and reused across all 16 states (S3b hoist); [n_ct,128,S] carried scan_state; per-seq-tile store
notes: PROMOTED, phase-3 best. Full 5-seed PASS (correct 1/1), 0.7278ms/1.729x (--fast screen 0.7273 consistent). BEATS the 1.608x ref_optimized reference and the promoted mamba_v2 (0.7822/1.609x) by ~7.1%; same-session mamba_v2 control 0.7839ms gives ~0.2% jitter, so the delta is ~35x the noise band. Math/fp32 semantics IDENTICAL to mamba_v1/v2 (S1a is a loop reorder + shared broadcast materialization; S3b hoists an already-computed state-independent product) -> rel-L2 unchanged. Engine shift PE 99->59% (broadcast halved), Vec 89->95% but its work cut ~20% by the deltaU hoist so wall-clock fell below the old PE=0.77ms floor. HBMrd stays 16MB. Key insight (Codex-suggested): S1a ALONE regressed (0.8397, Vec-exposed) but S1a+S3b together removes enough of the exposed Vec work to net a win -- the two levers are only worth landing combined.

structure: mamba_v4 (seq-tile-outer + shared b/c broadcast + hoisted deltaU) with nl.static_range full-unroll of the S=16 state loop and both n_channel_tile=2 channel loops; seq carry loop stays nl.sequential_range
notes: PROMOTED, phase-3 best. Full 5-seed PASS (correct 1/1), 0.7164ms/1.756x. S4 static-unroll of the compile-time-constant state/channel loops gives the compiler a longer dependency-free window. ~1.55% over mamba_v4: sub-3% but PROMOTED because the same-session A/B bands are fully non-overlapping (s4unroll 0.7162-0.7170 vs v4 0.7273-0.7280, ~0.1% internal jitter each, delta ~15x the jitter). Math/fp32 semantics unchanged (loop-kind change only). Also confirmed (v4 layout) the width optimum stays 512: v4_w256=0.7363, v4_w448=0.7248, v4(512)=0.7273 -- 448 nominally ~sub-noise but 512 kept (matches phase-1 sweep). Cumulative 0.832x(v1)->1.609x(v2)->1.729x(v4)->1.756x(v5).
S2 width re-sweep on the v4 layout (bitlesson: re-sweep after a layout shift). 256 regresses vs 512 (0.7363 vs 0.7273). Width optimum did NOT move off 512 after the S1a+S3b engine-balance shift.

S2 width re-sweep on the v4 layout. 448 nominally 0.7248 vs 512's 0.7273 (~0.3%, sub-noise); 512 kept for consistency with the phase-1 sweep and stability. Width optimum stays at the 448/512 flat band; no material move after the layout shift. Applied S4 unroll on the 512 winner (mamba_v5).
